blocks.text: 11.2 Introduction to gates
Following flow cytometry standards, the BactoSense uses gates to count cells in samples.
blocks.html: Following flow cytometry standards, the BactoSense uses gates to count cells in samples.

blocks.text: We define:
blocks.html: We define:

blocks.text: Gate: A line or polygon applied to a dotplot to quantify populations of measured cells. Set of gates, or gating set: A collection of two or more gates, used for the gating strategy. The types of gates are fixed, but users can change the limits of each gate. These are different for TCC and ICC measurements. Gating strategy: Defines how the gates are combined to count cells. For example, HNAC is the number of cells that are inside the TCC polygon and higher than the HNA lower limit. These strategies are different for TCC and ICC measurements.
blocks.html:
• Gate: A line or polygon applied to a dotplot to quantify populations of measured cells.
  • Set of gates, or gating set: A collection of two or more gates, used for the gating strategy. The types of gates are fixed, but users can change the limits of each gate. These are different for TCC and ICC measurements.
  • Gating strategy: Defines how the gates are combined to count cells. For example, HNAC is the number of cells that are inside the TCC polygon and higher than the HNA lower limit. These strategies are different for TCC and ICC measurements.

blocks.text: Gating sets are specific for a type of cartridge. As an example, only gating sets of type TCC can be used with measurements performed using a TCC cartridge.
blocks.html: Gating sets are specific for a type of cartridge. As an example, only gating sets of type TCC can be used with measurements performed using a TCC cartridge.

The BactoSense has preconfigured gating sets for all available cartridge types. These gating sets are called Default gating sets. They have been carefully designed to be applicable to the vast majority of samples.

blocks.text: 11.3 Cartridges, gates and result parameters

Depending on the cartridge used for a measurement, different parameters are measured. The subsections below describe gating sets and result parameters for TCC (Total Cell Count), ICC (Intact Cell Count), ACC (Active Cell Count), CBC (Coliform Cell Count), EBC (E. coli Cell Count), and NBC (Enterococcus Cell Count).
blocks.html: Depending on the cartridge used for a measurement, different parameters are measured. The subsections below describe gating sets and result parameters for TCC (Total Cell Count), ICC (Intact Cell Count), ACC (Active Cell Count), CBC (Coliform Cell Count), EBC (E. coli Cell Count), and NBC (Enterococcus Cell Count).

blocks.text: CBC, EBC and NBC cartridges are compatible with BactoSense ID and BactoSense SMART. Each uses selective enzymatic labelling and a single polygon gate, and reports one cell concentration. No HNA or activity subpopulations are calculated for these cartridges.
blocks.html: CBC, EBC and NBC cartridges are compatible with BactoSense ID and BactoSense SMART. Each uses selective enzymatic labelling and a single polygon gate, and reports one cell concentration. No HNA or activity subpopulations are calculated for these cartridges.

blocks.text: Interpreting CBC, EBC and NBC results CBC, EBC and NBC are cell concentrations expressed in cells per millilitre (1/mL). Cell counts and culture results expressed in colony-forming units (CFU) measure different properties of a sample and cannot be compared directly.
blocks.html:
INTERPRETING CBC, EBC AND NBC RESULTS

CBC, EBC and NBC are cell concentrations expressed in cells per millilitre (1/mL). Cell counts and culture results expressed in colony-forming units (CFU) measure different properties of a sample and cannot be compared directly.

blocks.text: 11.4 Change gates
11.4.1 Regate measurements
Regating is the process of applying a different gating set to existing measurement data.
blocks.html: Regating is the process of applying a different gating set to existing measurement data.

blocks.text: A prerequisite for regating is the presence of such additional gating set. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Gate settings to view the available gating sets. The process of modifying an existing gating set is described in Edit existing gating sets .
blocks.html:
• A prerequisite for regating is the presence of such additional gating set. On the Home screen, press Settings, then Gate settings to view the available gating sets.
  • The process of modifying an existing gating set is described in Edit existing gating sets.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. 2. Press Logs, then Results (manual mode) or Results (online mode), depending on how the measurement was performed. 3. To regate a single measurement, select the measurement to see the result details page. To regate multiple measurements (batch), long-press on the measurement, until it is highlighted and a check box appears on the left. Then tap on more measurement to also select them for regating. 4. Press Re-gate result in the single-result view, or Re-gate when several measurements are selected. 5. Select the desired gating set by checking its box. 6. Press the Confirm button to start the regating process. Additional information Depending on the number of measurements, regating can take several minutes. 7. After finishing, press OK.

New gating sets can be created either from a copy of an existing gating set, or from scratch.

blocks.text: Creating a new gating set from a copy
blocks.html: Creating a new gating set from a copy

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGES 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Gate settings button. 3. Make sure the gating type (e.g. TCC, ICC) matches with your target application. 4. Press the Copy icon to create a copy of the gating set. 5. In the newly generated copy, press the Edit icon and follow the editing instructions in Edit existing gating sets .

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Gate settings button. 3. Press the Edit button of the gate you wish to edit. 4. Change the name if desired, then press the Next button. 5. Adjust the number and position of polygon corners (for TCC and ICC refer to Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC ). A polygon gate can have between 3 and 6 corners. 6. Press the Next button. 7. Enter the HNA lower limit (for TCC and ICC refer to Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC ). 8. Press Save. In the save dialog, choose Save to update the existing set, or Save as new set to keep the original and create a new set. 9. After finishing, you can select the modified gating set when creating new measurements, or regate existing measurements, as described in Regate measurements .

1.As an Advanced or Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu.
2.Press the Gate settings button.
3.Press the Edit button of the gate you wish to edit.
4.Change the name if desired, then press the Next button.
5.Adjust the number and position of polygon corners (for TCC and ICC refer to Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC). A polygon gate can have between 3 and 6 corners.
6.Press the Next button.
7.Enter the HNA lower limit (for TCC and ICC refer to Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC).
8.Press Save. In the save dialog, choose Save to update the existing set, or Save as new set to keep the original and create a new set.
9.After finishing, you can select the modified gating set when creating new measurements, or regate existing measurements, as described in Regate measurements.

blocks.text: 11.4.4 Strategy to adjust gates for TCC and ICC

The BactoSense is delivered with default gate sets that are suitable for the vast majority of samples. If needed however, advanced users have the possibility to adjust the gate. A general procedure to adjust the gate is explained below and is valid for both TCC and ICC cartridges.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. Measure a water sample using the standard Water analysis protocol. On the Result details page, the FL1 vs FL2 dotplot shows: 1) LNA and HNA cells in the water 2) Electrical noise from the optical detectors 3) Debris/background noise (This can include damaged cells, aggregates or other particles) 2. On the Home screen, press Settings to open the settings menu. Press the Gate settings button. 3. Depending on your needs, perform one of the following: • Create a new set of gates • Edit an existing set of gates • Copy an existing set of gates and edit the copy 4. Give a name to this set of gates and press Next. 5. Place the polygon gate at each extremity (left and right). For example, use these four points: FL1 FL2 3.0 0.0 3.0 6.1 6.5 6.1 6.5 0.0 6. Select the gate you just created, and re- process the data with the new gate by pressing the button Confirm. 10. If needed, for the FL2 axis, place the points “b” and “c” of the gate just below the debris/background area (generally appearing as straight diagonals). 12. Save the adjusted gate. 13. blocks.text: 11.5 Advanced data analysis

BactoSense measurement data can be exported in Flow Cytometry Standard (FCS) 3.1 file format. The FCS file format is standardized by the International Society for Advancement of Cytometry (ISAC) to ensure interoperability between different flow cytometry instruments and analysis software. There are different versions of the FCS format with each version introducing improvements and additional features. FCS data can be used for custom offline postprocessing, such as the application of complex gating strategies, “microbial fingerprinting”, automated anomaly detection and many more.

blocks.text: 11.6 Comparison with other flow cytometers

To compare results of the BactoSense to another flow cytometer, a reference solution containing auto fluorescent beads can be analyzed. This method allows the user to compare the measurement scales of different devices.
blocks.html: To compare results of the BactoSense to another flow cytometer, a reference solution containing auto fluorescent beads can be analyzed. This method allows the user to compare the measurement scales of different devices.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. It is recommended to use the Validation Kit which contains a ready to use beads solution. Read the instructions of the Validation Kit for more information. 2. Install the manual sampling device according to the user manual. 3. Take of one of the Validation kit’s beads solutions and load it into the sampling device. Read the instructions of the Validation Kit for more information. 4. Additional information Press the Home button. Press the Back button as many times as needed for the Home button to appear. 5. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 6. Select Prime from the protocol list. See Performing a Prime . 7. Press the Next and Start button. Let the priming protocol finish. 8. Press New, choose Beads Analysis from the list, then press Next and Start. 9. Wait for the results and if necessary, precisely adjust the gate of the FL1 vs FL2 dot plot to count only the 4 populations of beads. It is important to ensure that noise, background, and debris are not counted into the gate. See Edit existing gating sets to adjust the gate. 10. On the FL1 vs counts histogram, estimate the log value of each peak’s center on the FL1 axis. In this example, we obtain approximately (in log): 1 st peak = 4.05 2 nd peak = 4.3 3 rd peak = 5.35 4 th peak = 6.2 11. Measure the same beads with the other flow cytometer you want to compare and repeat the steps 10 and 11. In this example, we obtain approximately (in log): 1 st peak = log(10 3 ) = 3 2 nd peak = log(2 10 3 ) = 3.3 3 rd peak = log(2.4 10 4 ) = 4.4 4 th peak = log(1.6*10 5 ) = 5.2 12. With the different values obtained for both devices, it is now possible to compare their scales and their measurement windows.
